{"tool":"write_file","arguments":{"path":"final_report.md","content":"# Finding: Log Injection in Audit Logs

## Description
The application writes user-controlled data (specifically display names) directly into the local audit log files without proper sanitization or encoding. Because the input is not checked for carriage return (`\r`) or line feed (`\n`) characters, an attacker can inject arbitrary log entries. This can be used to forge audit trails, mislead administrators, or mask malicious activity by simulating legitimate system events.

## Evidence
Based on the source code analysis, the audit logging mechanism concatenates user-provided strings directly into the log stream. A payload containing REDACTED_TRIGGER allows an attacker to start a new line in the log file, effectively creating a fake log entry that appears indistinguishable from a system-generated one.

## Fix Guidance
To remediate this vulnerability, implement one of the following strategies:
1. **Newline Escaping**: Sanitize all user-controlled input by replacing or escaping newline characters before writing to the log.
2. **Structured Logging**: Transition from plain-text logs to a structured format (e.g., JSON). This ensures that the log aggregator treats the entire entry as a single record regardless of the content.
3. **Logging Framework**: Use a mature logging library that automatically handles escaping or provides built-in protection against injection."}}

# Finding: Log Injection in Audit Logs

## Description
The application writes user-controlled data (specifically display names) directly into the local audit log files without proper sanitization or encoding. Because the input is not checked for carriage return (`\r`) or line feed (`\n`) characters, an attacker can inject arbitrary log entries. This can be used to forge audit trails, mislead administrators, or mask malicious activity by simulating legitimate system events.

## Evidence
Based on the source code analysis, the audit logging mechanism concatenates user-provided strings directly into the log stream. A payload containing REDACTED_TRIGGER allows an attacker to start a new line in the log file, effectively creating a fake log entry that appears indistinguishable from a system-generated one.

## Fix Guidance
To remediate this vulnerability, implement one of the following strategies:
1. **Newline Escaping**: Sanitize all user-controlled input by replacing or escaping newline characters before writing to the log.
2. **Structured Logging**: Transition from plain-text logs to a structured format (e.g., JSON). This ensures that the log aggregator treats the entire entry as a single record regardless of the content.
3. **Logging Framework**: Use a mature logging library that automatically handles escaping or provides built-in protection against injection.
